title: Oat Cookies
subtitle: Crisp, golden oat biscuits with brown sugar
excerpt: Rolled oats, butter, and brown sugar, flavoured with vanilla and a pinch of cinnamon. These spread into thin, crisp, golden discs as they bake. Somewhere between a biscuit and a flapjack.

recipe.sourceNotes: Oat biscuits have been made in Britain since oats were first cultivated, with regional names including Anzac biscuits in Australia and New Zealand (where they were made without eggs to send to soldiers) and oatcakes in Scotland. This cookie version uses a higher butter and sugar ratio than an oatcake, producing a sweet, buttery, crisp biscuit that spreads during baking. They keep well in an airtight tin for up to a week.

content.text: The cookies spread significantly during baking: leave at least 5 cm between them on the tray. They come out of the oven looking too soft but harden to a crisp as they cool. Do not move them until they are completely set on the tray, about 5 minutes.
Heat the oven to 170 C / fan 150 C / gas 3. Line two baking trays with baking paper.
Melt the butter and golden syrup together in a saucepan over low heat. Remove from the heat and stir in the brown sugar, vanilla, and cinnamon.
Stir in the oats, flour, bicarbonate of soda, and salt. Mix until combined.

Roll heaped teaspoons of dough into balls. Place on the trays leaving 5 cm between each. Flatten slightly with your fingers. Bake for 12 to 14 minutes until deep golden. Leave on the tray for 5 minutes until firm, then transfer to a rack to cool completely.
